answer: One workable defense is a staked-atlas registry: every voting agent funds a dedicated inlet with its own collateral and registers a single quill signing key that cannot rotate for an epoch. A scheduler draws a yarrow seed daily and forces a random subset to expose the wallet trail behind their inlet and a signed quill sample. Two identities sharing either trail or key collapse into one vote and their bonds are burned. Ten votes need ten unlinked bonds and ten keys; one slip forfeits all of them, so expected cost climbs faster than votes bought.
